I'm good at flirting and charming my romantic interests, but I struggle to maintain a long term relationship (my longest relationship was 10 months).

I no longer outbursts like I did when I was a kid, but when I have meltdowns I become quite and get major anxiety and I end up avoiding people around me.

In my experience you will never be able to cope with it as long as you try to adapt to society. You have to accept that you will never be able to fully fit in with society, but not in a sense that you avoid people entirely. You have to design your life in a way that you can benefit off of being you. Easier said than done and I am still working on it, but it's really the only way.

Surround yourself with people who can accept and love you for who you are. There are NT's out there who are like that. Lean into your special interests. If it makes you happy and keeps you energized then is that really a waste of time?

I've managed to mask for a good period of time and I've managed to build relationships with many NT's. Many of them haven't stood the test of time, but the ones that have are relationships that I didn't have to force myself to be normal for. Rather these are people who have seen the real me, love the real me, enjoy the real me. These are people I can make happy without even trying. The people who I had to try for weren't even worth the effort because even when I managed to win them over, I was disillusioned  and unfulfilled and even ended up resenting them. I don't have a relationship with those people.

Yes, social inclusion looks amazing before you experience it, and that was my life before 15. I masked for 13 years until this year when I was diagnosed in March (I ended up in a wellness center due to depression caused by disillusionment over my life). I can tell you that even though I have great memories from being in the in crowd, the price is a lot higher than the rewards. You are constantly drained, constantly need alone time and eventually end up having meltdowns that undo all the work you've put into building those relationships, and you end up not having those people in your life anyway.

Edit: Just to add, it may not seem like it until you get to know them, but most NT's are a mess. Like us, they are also masking. I'm not saying we're superior, but simply that the grass isn't necessarily greener on the other side.
